docs.title: probcal
docs.text:
Post-hoc probability calibration and calibration governance for binary classifiers: the evidence a regulated PD model needs alongside the map itself. The core is numpy-only; everything else is an optional extra.

One deployed calibration runs a loop, and probcal covers all of it: calibrate → evaluate → invert and decide → monitor → act → report, then back to re-anchoring. The How it works page draws that loop once, in one view.

Calibrate. Thirteen calibrators: Platt, temperature, beta, isotonic, centered isotonic, histogram binning, scaling-binning, BBQ, ENIR, Venn–Abers (IVAP and CVAP), spline, and segmented. With them come a rigid, auditable logit offset, automatic selection under nested cross-validation, and prefit / cross-validation data flows. Choose a calibrator is the catalog.

Evaluate. Proper scores, binned and binning-free calibration errors, the CORP decomposition, per-grade supervisory backtests, calibration belts, reliability curves on both probability and logit scales, grouped evaluation by segment, and conservatism tooling for low-default portfolios (Pluto–Tasche most-prudent PDs, Jeffreys upper bands, margin-of-conservatism offsets).

Decide. Exact and generalized inverses turn a policy PD into a raw-score cutoff or a whole masterscale, refusing unattainable targets instead of clamping. Set cutoffs and invert maps.

Monitor and act. Anytime-valid monitoring runs on an e-process whose alarm keeps its type-I guarantee at every look. It localizes the onset of drift and issues a recommendation that can be applied as a new offset, on the record. Monitor and act.

Prove it. JSON serialization (never pickle) with fingerprints and a golden-file compatibility promise, self-contained HTML reports, and one page tying the artifacts to what each of them actually proves: Auditability.

Integrate. scikit-learn (the bare core is a duck on ≥ 1.6; an adapter covers the probability-matrix world), optbinning scorecards (calibrated PDs carried back to the points scale), and treecf counterfactuals bound to a named calibrator.

pip install probcal

Three doors, by who is arriving:

  • New to calibration → Install and quickstart, then the 20-minute PD calibration walkthrough.
  • Validating someone's model → Auditability and Build a validation report.
  • Coming from scikit-learn → the three-tier sklearn guide.

Status: released on PyPI, beta. Until 1.0, breaking changes bump the minor version, are listed in the changelog with the reasoning, and keep an explicit escape hatch where the old behavior had legitimate uses; a deprecated symbol warns with a DeprecationWarning for at least one minor release before removal, naming its replacement. Serialized artifacts carry a stronger promise: every 0.x release reads schema 1, pinned by golden files in CI. The full surface and its conventions: API stability.

docs.title: API stability
docs.text: Status: beta on PyPI. Until 1.0, breaking changes bump the minor version, are listed in the changelog with the reasoning, and, where the old behavior had legitimate uses, keep an explicit escape hatch (the bins=None/grid_size=None pattern). Serialized artifacts have their own, stronger promise: every 0.x release reads schema 1, enforced by committed golden files in CI (see the Serialization chapter).

docs.title: Public surface
docs.text:
The public API is exactly the export lists below; anything prefixed with _ or not exported is internal and may change without notice.

  • probcal.__all__: the calibrators (PlattCalibrator, TemperatureCalibrator, BetaCalibrator, IsotonicCalibrator, CenteredIsotonicCalibrator, HistogramBinningCalibrator, ScalingBinningCalibrator, BBQCalibrator, ENIRCalibrator, VennAbersCalibrator, CrossVennAbersCalibrator, SplineCalibrator, SegmentedCalibrator), BaseCalibrator, UnattainableTargetError, CalibratorSelector, CalibratedModel, LogitOffset, OffsetEstimate, estimate_offset, offset_from_estimate, Chain, the reliability curves and calibration_belt, threshold translation (calibrated_interval_to_raw, calibrated_bands_to_raw), attribution repair, make_pd_portfolio, expit/logit, and the metrics/monitor submodules.
  • probcal.metrics.__all__: the 47-symbol metric catalog (proper scores, binned and binning-free calibration errors, per-grade backtests, the mixture-LR grade e-test, Pluto-Tasche most-prudent PDs, Jeffreys upper masterscale bands, the recalibration-regression framework, SKCE, evaluate).
  • probcal.monitor.__all__: CalibrationMonitor, MonitorStep, MonitorReport, AppliedAction, moc_offset, moc_offset_from_counts.
  • probcal.sklearn (extra probcal[sklearn]): SklearnCalibrator, SklearnOffset, CalibratedClassifier.
  • probcal.integrations.optbinning (extra probcal[optbinning]): calibrate_scorecard, CalibratedScorecard.
  • probcal.plots (extra probcal[viz]): the plotting catalog, including plot_e_process.
  • probcal.report (extra probcal[viz]): validation_report. Not re-exported from top-level probcal, so import probcal and import probcal.report both stay matplotlib-free at import time.

docs.title: Added in 0.3.0
docs.text:
New public symbols relative to 0.2.0, kept here as one running list for this release regardless of which chapter documents them (extend this list rather than starting a new one for later 0.3.0 additions):

  • estimate_offset, offset_from_estimate, OffsetEstimate (probcal): offset-only logistic MLE with a Fisher standard error; see Offset.
  • metrics.pluto_tasche, metrics.pluto_tasche_from_arrays, PlutoTascheResult: one-period most-prudent PDs; see Conservatism.
  • metrics.jeffreys_upper_bands: Jeffreys upper masterscale bands; see Conservatism.
  • monitor.moc_offset, monitor.moc_offset_from_counts: margin-of- conservatism offsets; see Conservatism and Monitoring.
  • metrics.hl_e_test, HlEResult: fixed-sample mixture-LR grade e-test (safe Hosmer–Lemeshow analogue); see Monitoring.
  • MonitorStep.grade_delta_ci: per-grade time-uniform confidence sequences. MonitorReport.onset_label and the CalibrationMonitor(recommendation_window=) keyword-only constructor parameter ("since_onset" default, "trailing" escape hatch) give drift-onset localization and the window it feeds into report()'s trailing diagnostics; see Monitoring.
  • CalibrationMonitor.apply_recommendation, monitor.AppliedAction: closes the report-to-action loop for kind="re-offset"; see Monitoring.
  • SegmentedCalibrator (probcal): empirical-Bayes (DerSimonian-Laird) shrunken per-segment logit offsets on top of a shared base map; see Segmented calibration.
  • metrics.evaluate(by=) and GroupedMetricReport (metric catalog 46 → 47 symbols): per-group metric reports plus a pooled report; plots. plot_reliability(by=) adds the matching faceted reliability grid; see the new Grouped evaluation guide.
  • metrics.ecce(presorted=): keyword-only throughput switch (default False) declaring p already sorted ascending, so the internal sort is skipped; evaluate's bootstrap sorts each replicate once and shares that order. Results are unchanged when the declaration holds; see Metrics' "Computational cost".
  • probcal.report.validation_report: a self-contained HTML/markdown validation report (reliability, the metric report, the CORP decomposition, and, when given, the rating-grades, grouped-evaluation, monitoring, and calibrator-appendix sections); see the new Validation report guide.
  • corp_reliability (probcal, curves), CorpResult: the CORP (consistent, optimally binned, reproducible) reliability diagram and its exact score == mcb - dsc + unc decomposition; reliability_smooth (probcal, curves), KernelReliabilityCurve is a fourth reliability construction sharing smooth_ece's fixed-point bandwidth exactly; see the new CORP and score decomposition chapter.
  • plots.plot_corp, plots.plot_mcb_dsc, plots.plot_attributes, plots.plot_murphy: four new plotting functions (CORP reliability, the MCB-DSC plane, the Hsu & Murphy attributes diagram, and Murphy diagrams); see Visualization and the new CORP and score decomposition chapter.
  • metrics.murphy_curve, MurphyCurve (metric catalog 38 → 40 symbols): the Ehm, Gneiting, Jordan & Krüger (2016) elementary-score decomposition underlying plots.plot_murphy; see Metrics and tests and Visualization.
  • BaseCalibrator.__sklearn_is_fitted__ and BaseCalibrator.__sklearn_tags__ (also __sklearn_is_fitted__ on Chain, LogitOffset and CalibratedModel): sklearn's duck-typing hooks, so a bare calibrator works with clone, get_tags, check_is_fitted and CV loops on sklearn >= 1.6 without the adapter; sklearn is imported inside __sklearn_tags__ only, so import probcal stays numpy-only. See the sklearn guide.

docs.title: Added in 0.3.1
docs.text:
New public symbols and behavior relative to 0.3.0, kept here as one running list for this release regardless of which chapter documents them:

  • _validation.validate_scores accepts a two-column probability matrix ((n, 2), entries in [0, 1], rows summing to 1 within 1e-6), inherited everywhere scores enter the package — every calibrator, LogitOffset, Chain, the metric catalog, and probcal.sklearn's probability mode; see the sklearn guide.
  • Chain(stages) accepts unfitted stages, and Chain.fit(s, y, sample_weight=None) fits them sequentially (supersedes the 0.3.0 note that a chain composes only fitted stages); get_params/set_params gain stages__i__param nesting. See the sklearn guide.
  • SklearnOffset (probcal.sklearn): a TransformerMixin/BaseEstimator wrapping LogitOffset; see the new "Stacking an offset" section of the sklearn guide.
  • positive_column keyword-only parameter on SklearnCalibrator and SklearnOffset, plus the orientation UserWarning fired at fit; see the sklearn guide.
  • LogitOffset.fit(y=) keyword-only parameter, accepted and ignored, giving Chain.fit's sequential protocol one call shape across stages.

docs.title: Conventions that will not silently change
docs.text:
• New parameters are keyword-only; fitted attributes end in _.
  • import probcal depends on numpy and the standard library only, enforced by a test rather than by review.
  • No silent clamps or approximations: numeric shortcuts keep an exact escape hatch; refusals name the reason and the alternative (UnattainableTargetError doctrine).
  • Serialization is JSON, never pickle.

docs.title: Deprecation policy
docs.text:
Pre-1.0: a deprecated symbol warns (DeprecationWarning) for at least one minor release before removal, with the replacement named in the warning and the changelog. Behavioral changes that alter numbers ship with a detailed changelog entry and, where feasible, a parameter that recovers the old values.

0.3.0 deprecated nothing: every new symbol above is additive, and no existing symbol carries a DeprecationWarning; the policy stood unused this release.

docs.title: scikit-learn estimator checks
docs.text:
sklearn.utils.estimator_checks generates multi-column feature matrices of arbitrary reals. Its data model contains no score-level estimator, so most of the corpus cannot be run against SklearnCalibrator at all, the same kind of domain restriction imbalanced-learn declares for its resamplers. Those checks are declared inapplicable through sklearn's own mechanism (expected_failed_checks on 1.6+, _more_tags()["_xfail_checks"] below it), each entry naming the data that check generates and which part of the score-level contract it violates. They are inapplicable, not known failures; the checks whose data the contract does admit run live and pass.

Every inapplicable check with a score-level analogue is re-implemented on valid (n,) probability data in tests/test_sklearn_mirror_checks.py: fit idempotence, no mutation of the passed arrays, __dict__ unchanged by the predict-side methods, pickle (adapter) and JSON (core) round trips, clone-then-fit, subset and sample-order invariance, and integer sample_weight equal to row duplication over every registered calibrator class, with the exceptions (CV- and quantile-based internals) named in a table together with their measured tolerance. Checks with no analogue at all (multiclass, pairwise, sparse) are listed in that module's docstring with one line each. The score-level contract itself is pinned by tests/test_calibrator_protocol.py.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Rendered from the numpy-style docstrings, split across three pages (a single page with all modules triggers a third-party rendering pathology):

  • Calibrators: the base contract and all thirteen calibrators.
  • Metrics and tests: the full probcal.metrics catalog and evaluate.
  • Tools: offset, wrapper, selection, curves, plots, attribution, thresholds, datasets.

The public surface is exported flat from probcal; metrics live under probcal.metrics.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

Format: Keep a Changelog; versioning: SemVer.
No breaking changes: every previously accepted input and object behaves identically.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Two-column probability-matrix input, core-wide. _validation.validate_scores now accepts an (n, 2) array whose entries lie in [0, 1] and whose rows sum to 1 within 1e-6 absolute tolerance, returning column 1 — the exact shape every predict_proba call in the ecosystem hands back. Every calibrator's fit/predict_proba/point_inverse, LogitOffset, Chain, the whole metric catalog, and probcal.sklearn's probability-input mode inherit the rule from this one shared validator, with a single unified rejection message replacing the old one. Pinned bit-for-bit by tests/test_validation.py (all 14 registered calibrators plus both LogitOffset modes) and by the two-column kinds added to the mirror-check suite.
  • Fittable Chain (supersedes the 0.3.0 note that a chain composes only fitted stages). Chain(stages) now accepts unfitted stages — construction validates only their types and order — and gains Chain.fit(s, y, sample_weight=None), which fits the head calibrator and then each offset in turn on the running calibrated probabilities; every stage is always refit, so composing already-fitted objects is how a stage stays frozen. stages is stored verbatim; calibrator_/offsets_ are now read-only properties, and every reading method raises the standard not-fitted RuntimeError before a fit. get_params/set_params gain stages__i__param nesting (LogitOffset also gained get_params/set_params to support it), and the serialization payload is unchanged — goldens are byte-identical. Both sklearn adapters clone the calibrator prototype via sklearn.base.clone, so SklearnCalibrator(calibrator=Chain([...])) and CalibratedClassifier(calibrator=Chain([...])) now work with an unfitted chain. Tests: tests/test_chain.py, tests/test_sklearn_duck.py, tests/test_sklearn_offset.py.
  • SklearnOffset. probcal.sklearn.SklearnOffset(delta=None, target_mean=None, *, positive_column=1) (TransformerMixin/BaseEstimator): fit(X, y=None, sample_weight=None) fits an inner offset_ (LogitOffset); transform returns the shifted (n, 1) column, predict_proba the (n, 2) matrix, and to_dict delegates to the fitted LogitOffset's payload. Runs the sklearn estimator checks against its own OFFSET_XFAIL_CHECKS inapplicability table, mirrored in the mirror-check suite. Tests: tests/test_sklearn_offset.py. Docs: guide/sklearn.md's new "Stacking an offset" section.
  • positive_column. A keyword-only parameter on SklearnCalibrator and SklearnOffset naming which column of a two-column input is the positive class. At fit, when the estimator also has y (the calibrator, not the offset), a one-shot UserWarning fires if the selected column's event mean is below the non-event mean, naming the flip as the likely fix — probcal warns, it never auto-flips; input="logit" stays single-column, since a logit matrix has no sum rule to check orientation against. n_features_in_ (1 or 2) is recorded at fit and enforced at predict.
  • LogitOffset.fit(y=). fit gains an optional keyword-only y=None, accepted and ignored in both explicit-delta and target-mean modes, giving Chain.fit's sequential fit protocol one call shape across calibrator and offset stages.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Calibrators and offsets were unusable directly after a predict_proba-shaped pipeline step — a bare (n, 2) matrix from model.predict_proba(X) raised in every fit/predict_proba call across the package, forcing a manual column slice before every calibration call. The two-column input rule above removes that friction end to end; new tests/test_lightgbm.py (importorskip-gated on sklearn/lightgbm; the CI integrations job now installs lightgbm) pins the fix against a real LGBMClassifier.predict_proba matrix flowing through SklearnCalibrator and SklearnOffset in one Pipeline.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Reader-oriented documentation reorganization. The nav now answers "who is arriving" — Learn (install, how it works, the 20-minute walkthrough), Guide (task-ordered along the calibrate → evaluate → invert/decide → monitor → act → report lifecycle, with the integrations beside it), Concepts (regrouped theory) — and the front page states that lifecycle once, linking each stage to its guide page. No page changed URL. Three assembled guide pages are new: guide/choosing.md (the calibrator catalog, every factual column naming the test that pins it), guide/cutoffs.md (policy PD → raw cutoff → masterscale → recourse), and guide/auditability.md (artifact → what it proves → how to verify it, plus a worked reviewer session). Every Python block in the docs is now executed page by page against a fixed data vocabulary (tests/test_docs_snippets.py, convention in docs/README.md), so snippets rot loudly rather than silently. Figure coverage is complete: every function in probcal.plots has a committed, alt-texted figure on a prose page — the e-process trajectory with its per-grade panel in concepts/monitoring.md and the faceted reliability grid in guide/groups.md were the two gaps. guide/report.md links and shows a full sample validation report (docs/assets/sample_validation_report.html, regenerated by docs/scripts/generate_sample_report.py). tests/test_docs_structure.py holds the structure to all of it: the 0.3.0 sitemap stays a subset of the new one, the front page keeps naming every capability, no plot function loses its figure.
  • guide/sklearn.md: each tier now states its input shape (scores (n,), (n, 1), or a predict_proba matrix (n, 2)), the single-column contract sentence is extended to cover the two-column case, positive_column, and the orientation warning, and a new "Stacking an offset" section covers the two ways to compose an offset — a single Chain step, or a separate SklearnOffset step with its own governance lifecycle (swapped in from apply_recommendation's output without touching the calibrator). guide/monitoring.md gains a "Re-offsetting inside a pipeline" subsection with the matching SklearnOffset replacement snippet. concepts/offset.md gains a paragraph on Chain.fit's sequential fitting: stages fit on the same calibration data, the offset anchoring the calibrator's in-sample output exactly as CalibratedModel.offset_to does — no cross-fitting, no automatic MLE offset.

No breaking API changes — the second stability minor on the road to 1.0: every 0.2.0 call and serialized file keeps working, the 0.2.0 goldens are verified unchanged in CI, the one default-behaviour change (CalibrationMonitor.report()'s post-alarm window, see Changed) has the recommendation_window="trailing" escape hatch, and a weighted PlattCalibrator fit — the one case that was ever wrong — now differs from 0.2.0 (see Fixed); every unweighted fit, and hence every default and golden file, is unchanged.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Grouped evaluation. metrics.evaluate(..., by=None) (metric catalog 46 → 47 symbols, count updated in docs/api-stability.md) and new GroupedMetricReport(pooled, groups, reports, counts) (_results.py, re-exported from probcal.metrics): grouping labels one per observation, by=None (default) is the existing report, byte-identical to 0.2.0 (pinned by a hard-coded fixture in tests/test_evaluate_groups.py); given by, each sorted label gets its own report — group i (sorted order) computed with seed + 1000 * i, a fixed label-independent offset, via a plain recursive evaluate() call on that group's slice, so grouped results are always identical to calling evaluate() by hand on the same slice — plus a pooled report on the full data using seed unchanged. A single-outcome-class group re-raises _prep's ValueError naming the group (f"group {g!r}: {msg}"). GroupedMetricReport.to_frame() follows the MonitorReport.to_frame pattern: a list of {group, metric, value, ci_low, ci_high} dicts, or a pandas DataFrame when pandas is importable. This is side-by-side reporting only — no cross-group comparison or multiplicity correction is computed; group-conditional calibration testing is explicitly out of scope and left as future work (docs/guide/groups.md). plots.plot_reliability(..., by=None) gains the matching faceted view: given by (y/p then required), it draws a min(3, G+1)-column grid of reliability_binned panels — one per sorted group plus a leading "pooled" panel, each rebuilt fresh from that group's data (curve is ignored for the panels) — on shared x/y axes via recursive light-panel calls (rug=False, annotate=False), and returns the Figure rather than an Axes (like plot_comparison); the by=None default path is untouched, pinned by tests/test_plots_regression.py. New guide chapter guide/groups.md (nav'd under Guide) and a paragraph in concepts/metrics.md's bootstrap-protocol section
  • Validation reports. probcal.report.validation_report(y, p, *, calibrator=None, monitor=None, grades=None, by=None, title=None, path=None, format="html", n_boot=200, seed=42) -> str (new src/probcal/report.py): a self-contained validation document assembled entirely from the existing public API — no new statistics are computed here. format="html" (default) is a single file with every figure embedded as a base64 PNG data URI (no <script>, no http(s):// links); format="markdown" writes GFM tables and PNG figure files to <path stem>_figures/ next to path (required in this mode), referenced with relative image links. Sections are omitted, not left blank, when their input is absent: reliability (curves.corp_reliability + plots.plot_corp, and curves.reliability_smooth + plots.plot_reliability(smooth=..., stats=True)), the metrics.evaluate table, and the CORP Brier/log-loss decomposition always render (they need only y/p); the rating-grades section (Jeffreys per-grade backtest and chart, Pluto-Tasche most-prudent PD, Jeffreys upper masterscale bands — all three ordered best to worst by mean predicted probability, stated in the section) renders when grades is given; the grouped-evaluation section (plots.plot_reliability(by=) panel plus the pooled-and-per-group metric table) when by is given; the monitoring section (plots.plot_e_process plus report().recommendation/reasoning/onset_label) when monitor is given; and the calibrator appendix (a collapsible <details> with calibrator.to_json() plus calibrator.interpret() messages) when calibrator is given. n_boot/seed are keyword-only and drive every resampling site in the report (metrics.evaluate, curves.corp_reliability, curves.reliability_smooth) from one shared knob, making the whole document one deterministic, reproducibly-costed call: two builds from the same inputs and seed are byte-identical apart from the single Generated ... UTC timestamp line. Import cost is the same discipline as the rest of the package: import probcal.report is stdlib + numpy + probcal only (matplotlib is imported lazily, only inside the figure-rendering path, the first time a figure actually renders — pinned by a subprocess test importing the module and asserting matplotlib is absent from sys.modules); calling validation_report itself still needs the [viz] extra (every report renders at least one figure), and its ImportError without it names probcal[viz]. Every caller-supplied label (group/grade names, monitor recommendation/onset strings, the title) is HTML-escaped, or GFM-cell-escaped in format="markdown" tables, before interpolation. Deliberately not re-exported from top-level probcal — reachable only as probcal.report.validation_report — so import probcal stays exactly as matplotlib-free as before. New guide chapter guide/report.md (nav'd under Guide)
  • Segmented calibration. probcal.SegmentedCalibrator(base=None, *, unseen="global") (new src/probcal/segmented.py, registered and re-exported from probcal): empirical-Bayes shrunken per-segment logit offsets on top of a shared base map. Fits base (default BetaCalibrator(), cloned via the wrapper.py type(base)(**base.get_params()) pattern) on all data as base_, then per segment g an offset-only logistic MLE against base_'s predictions (offset.estimate_offset, catching the single-outcome-class ValueError as delta_hat=0.0, se=inf — fully shrunk); the between-segment heterogeneity variance tau2 is the DerSimonian & Laird (1986) method-of-moments estimator (tau2=0 when fewer than two segments have a finite se), and each segment's shrunk offset is delta_tilde = delta_hat * tau2/(tau2+se**2) — a noisy small segment shrinks toward the base map, a large precise one keeps most of its own estimate, and tau2=0 recovers complete pooling exactly. fit(s, y, sample_weight=None, *, segments=None) and predict_proba(s, *, segments=None) add a keyword-only segments argument on top of the base signature (segments=None is a single segment "__all__" at fit time and the plain base map, delta=0, at predict time — no signature break for the zero-argument protocol calls); an unseen segment label at predict/inverse time is delta=0 (unseen="global", default) or a ValueError (unseen="raise"). interval_inverse/point_inverse gain a keyword-only segment=None and build Chain([base_, LogitOffset(delta=delta_tilde_g)]) for the requested segment; affine_logit_coeffs_ is (a, b+delta_tilde) only for a single fitted segment, else None (no single affine map across segments). Chain has no segments= slot, so Chain([seg, ...]) always predicts through seg's global map — documented as a limitation, not a bug. Fully serializable (_STATE_ATTRS/_state/_set_state, _params_for_dict/_params_from_dict storing an unfitted base as a {class, params} spec since an unfitted calibrator has no to_dict); new golden tests/golden/SegmentedCalibrator.json. Verified by simulation (docs/scripts/segmented_sim.py::recovery, full-size table in concepts/segmented.md, 2000 runs): on a 6-segment scenario with true offsets spread -0.6..+0.6 and sizes 30..3000, mean MSE 0.1242 for empirical Bayes versus 0.2354 (no pooling) and 0.1680 (complete pooling); on an all-zero-spread scenario at n=3000, max|mean delta_tilde| = 0.0003, i.e. shrinkage degrades gracefully to complete pooling. A reduced-size gate runs in CI (tests/test_segmented_sim.py, pytest.mark.slow). New chapter concepts/segmented.md
  • Closing the monitoring loop. CalibrationMonitor.apply_recommendation(target=None) -> AppliedAction (new monitor.AppliedAction, re-exported from probcal.monitor): closes the report-to-action loop for kind="re-offset" — estimates the log-odds shift by maximum likelihood (offset.estimate_offset) on the same window report()'s trailing diagnostics use (_recommendation_window_start, factored out of report() so the two windows can never disagree), composes the fitted LogitOffset onto target (Chain([target.calibrator_, *target.offsets_, offset]) for a Chain, copy.deepcopy(target).offset_to(delta=est.delta) for a CalibratedModel, None for no target — target itself is never mutated), and returns a fresh CalibrationMonitor with the same constructor parameters (new _ctor_params() helper, also used by to_dict) to watch the corrected pipeline — fresh rather than continued because the old e-process is a martingale under the null that the old forecast is calibrated, which no longer holds once the pipeline changes. kind="re-fit"/"none" return no offset, composed target, or fresh monitor — automatic re-fitting stays out of scope by design. AppliedAction carries kind, offset, composed, monitor, the window of batch labels used, and an audit dict of fingerprints and the estimated delta/se; it is itself serializable (to_dict/from_dict/to_json/from_json/fingerprint, nesting offset/composed/monitor as their own envelopes, with a composed CalibratedModel reattached via AppliedAction.from_dict(d, model=...) exactly as CalibratedModel.from_dict itself). mon is never mutated by the call. New section in concepts/monitoring.md
  • Drift-onset localization. CalibrationMonitor drift-onset estimate: each MonitorStep now records log_e_increment, the batch's additive plug-in log-LR contribution (the offset plug-in's bern_log_lr factor plus the shape plug-in's, each 0.0 when its plug-in is the identity) — unlike e_global, a logsumexp mixture that is not additive across batches, this series is purely additive and exists so drift onset can be localized. New monitor._onset.estimate_onset(increments) -> int is a backward-CUSUM argmax (k* = argmax_k sum_{j>=k} increments[j], ties resolving to the latest k) — an estimate, not a change-point test: no type-I control, no confidence set. report() runs it whenever an alarm has fired and exposes the result as the new MonitorReport.onset_label: str | None field, with a matching sentence appended to reasoning; steps loaded from a pre-0.3 payload carry log_e_increment = None (that payload records no increments), and a monitor holding any such step reports onset_label = None, says so in reasoning, and falls back to the "trailing" diagnostic window. Localization accuracy (batches built like docs/scripts/monitor_sim.py's, drift injected at batch 12 of 24 with shift=0.6, 40 seeded runs, tests/test_monitor_onset.py, pytest.mark.slow): median |onset - 12| = 1.0 (gate <= 2). New section in concepts/monitoring.md
  • Per-grade confidence sequences. CalibrationMonitor: each grade in a grade array now also gets its own time-uniform confidence sequence for its own offset — same construction and delta_ci_grid as the portfolio-level delta_ci, restricted to that grade's batch slice with the grade's own predictable plug-in as the alternative — surfaced as the new MonitorStep.grade_delta_ci: dict[str, tuple[float, float] | None] field (empty when no grades are given, and absent on steps loaded from a pre-0.3 payload, since it defaults to {}). This catches a single grade drifting while the portfolio-level offset CS stays put. plots.plot_e_process(report, *, grades_panel=False, ax=None) gains the keyword-only grades_panel: True adds a second axes (ax.figure.add_axes) plotting every grade's CS band across steps below the main plot; the default False call renders pixel-identically to 0.2.0 (tests/test_plots_regression.py). Serialization is additive and backward compatible: to_dict adds state["grade_cs_log"]/state["grade_cs_max"], from_dict reads them with .get(..., {}), and tests/test_monitor_grades.py::test_0_2_0_monitor_file_loads_and_continues pins that a 0.2.0 monitor payload still loads, its old steps carry an empty grade_delta_ci, and new batches with grade= populate it going forward. New section in concepts/monitoring.md
  • Per-grade e-test audit. metrics.hl_e_test(y, p, grades, *, mixture_grid=(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0), sample_weight=None) -> HlEResult (metric catalog 44 → 46 symbols, count updated in docs/api-stability.md): a fixed-sample, one-shot mixture-LR e-value audit per rating grade — for grade g, log E_g = logsumexp over the symmetrized mixture_grid (the same construction CalibrationMonitor's offset e-process uses, monitor._processes.bern_log_lr/logsumexp, with no predictable plug-in since a fixed sample has no strictly-earlier data to learn one from) of Σ_i log LR_i(sigma(logit(p_i) + delta) : p_i), minus log(2 * len(mixture_grid)); the test statistic is the product across grades, e_value = exp(Σ_g log E_g) (a valid e-value: each grade's mixture average has expectation 1 under H0 and grades are disjoint), p_value = min(1, 1 / e_value) by Markov's inequality. Named "mixture-LR grade e-test (safe Hosmer–Lemeshow analogue)": Henzi, Puke, Dimitriadis & Ziegel (2024) is cited in the docstring and concepts/monitoring.md as the paper that motivated a fixed-sample e-value analogue of Hosmer–Lemeshow, explicitly not as the implemented construction. Sample weights enter as exponents on the Bernoulli factors, same convention as the monitor. Verified by simulation (docs/scripts/hl_e_sim.py, full-size table in concepts/monitoring.md, wall time ≈ 19s for 2000 runs): type-I P(e >= 20) = 0.0025 (gate <= 0.0597), P(e >= 100) = 0.0005 (gate <= 0.0144), mean(e) = 0.4334 (gate <= 1 + 3*se); a reduced-size gate runs in CI (tests/test_hl_e_sim.py, pytest.mark.slow). Re-exported from probcal.metrics.grade.
  • Audited offset MLE. probcal.offset.estimate_offset(y, p, *, sample_weight=None) -> OffsetEstimate and probcal.offset.offset_from_estimate(est, p) -> LogitOffset (re-exported from top-level probcal): the offset-only logistic MLE of delta given realized outcomes, with a Fisher-information standard error, as the companion to LogitOffset's policy-driven mode B. The score equation sum(w * (y - sigma(logit(p) + delta))) = 0 is exactly LogitOffset(target_mean=mean_w(y))'s mean-matching condition, so estimate_offset shares its bisection root-finder (new _offset_mle helper) with probcal.monitor._processes.plug_in_delta — the two agree bit-for-bit on the same data; the standard error is 1 / sqrt(sum(w * q * (1 - q))) at the fitted q = sigma(logit(p) + delta). offset_from_estimate builds the same fitted LogitOffset mode A would give for delta=est.delta, so the audited MLE plugs directly into Chain, serialization, and the inverse maps. New section in concepts/offset.md
  • Margin-of-conservatism offsets. probcal.monitor.moc_offset(monitor_or_report, *, level=None) -> LogitOffset and probcal.monitor.moc_offset_from_counts(y, p, *, level=0.9, sample_weight=None) -> LogitOffset (new monitor/_actions.py; re-exported from probcal.monitor and top-level probcal): margin-of-conservatism offsets that turn monitoring evidence into an applied correction. moc_offset reads the upper end of CalibrationMonitor's time-uniform confidence sequence for the current offset (steps[-1].delta_ci[1] by default, or a level recomputed from the monitor's own running _cs_grid/_cs_max state) and returns a fitted LogitOffset(delta=hi) on the last monitored batch — a level requires the live monitor (TypeError for a frozen MonitorReport, which does not retain the running arrays), and an all-nulls-rejected delta_ci/surviving set raises ValueError pointing at delta_ci_grid. moc_offset_from_counts re-anchors p's mean at the one-sided Jeffreys posterior upper quantile of the observed event rate (beta_ppf(level, k + 0.5, n - k + 0.5), the same quantile jeffreys_grade_test/jeffreys_upper_bands use) via LogitOffset's existing mode B — no new numerics. New section in concepts/monitoring.md; monitor.__all__ gains both symbols.
  • Jeffreys masterscale bands. metrics.jeffreys_upper_bands(y, p, grades, *, level=0.9, order=None) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float]] (metric catalog 43 → 44 symbols, count updated in docs/api-stability.md): the per-grade Jeffreys posterior upper bound jeffreys_grade_test already reports as its own-grade display interval (beta_ppf(level, k_i + 0.5, n_i - k_i + 0.5), no cross-grade pooling), packaged as the {grade: (lo, hi)} masterscale band table thresholds.calibrated_bands_to_raw consumes directly — lo_i is the previous grade's hi (0.0 for the best grade), so the bands are contiguous by construction, and a zero-default grade still gets a strictly positive hi from the Jeffreys prior alone. The raw hi sequence is monotonized with _math.pava (weighted isotonic regression, weight = grade size) in the given order (default: grades sorted by mean p, best first), with a UserWarning fired only when PAVA actually changed something. Re-exported from probcal.metrics.grade; new section in concepts/conservatism.md
  • Pluto-Tasche most-prudent PDs. metrics.pluto_tasche(grade_n, grade_d, *, confidence=0.9, grades=None) -> PlutoTascheResult and metrics.pluto_tasche_from_arrays(grades, y, *, order, confidence=0.9, sample_weight=None) (metric catalog 40 → 43 symbols, count updated in docs/api-stability.md): the Pluto & Tasche (2005) one-period most-prudent PD for ordered rating grades — for grade i (best to worst, in the given order), pool its own obligors/defaults with every worse grade's (n*_i = sum(n[i:]), d*_i = sum(d[i:]), the rating-monotonicity assumption doing the work) and take the one-sided Clopper-Pearson upper bound of the pooled rate (_math.beta_ppf(confidence, d*_i + 1, n*_i - d*_i); d* == n* gives 1.0, a pooled n* == 0 raises); pluto_tasche_from_arrays aggregates observation-level (grades, y) into the same counts, weighted when sample_weight is given, and accepts an all-zero y (unlike most probcal metrics) since that is Pluto-Tasche's central use case. pd_upper is replaced by its cumulative maximum best to worst (np.maximum.accumulate, a prudent hull that can only raise a bound, never lower one) to guarantee it stays non-decreasing — a no-op on realistic, already rating-monotone data, PlutoTascheResult.monotonized reports whether it fired. Both functions are re-exported from probcal.metrics.grade, alongside the per-grade backtests they complement. Verified by simulation (docs/scripts/conservative_sim.py, full-size table in the new concepts/conservatism.md): minimum per-grade coverage 0.9225 at confidence 0.9 (gate 0.8866) and 0.9610 at 0.95 (gate 0.9403), 2000 runs; a reduced-size gate runs in CI (tests/test_conservative_sim.py, pytest.mark.slow)
  • CORP reliability diagrams. curves.corp_reliability(y, p, *, sample_weight=None, bands="consistency", level=0.9, n_resamples=200, random_state=42) -> CorpResult: the CORP (consistent, optimally binned, reproducible) reliability diagram of Dimitriadis, Gneiting & Jordan (2021) — the PAV (pool-adjacent-violators) recalibration map of y on p, weighted throughout (isotonic._aggregate_ties pools tied scores, _math.pava runs the weighted merge sweep, so an unweighted call is the w=1 special case of the same code path) — plus the exact score == mcb - dsc + unc decomposition of both the Brier score and log loss into uncertainty (the constant-forecast ceiling), discrimination (the PAV fit's improvement on it), and miscalibration (the raw score's shortfall against the PAV fit); log loss clips predictions and PAV levels to [1e-12, 1 - 1e-12] (_corp._CLIP, matching _math.logit's clip) so degenerate 0/1 blocks stay finite. bands="consistency" (default) resamples y ~ Bernoulli(p) under the calibration null, "confidence" bootstraps (y, p, sample_weight) triples, None skips bands; both are pointwise, not simultaneous — docs/scripts/corp_sim.py's full-size coverage table (pasted into the new concepts/corp.md) reports the pointwise-vs-uniform gap directly, and tests/test_corp_sim.py (pytest.mark.slow) gates pointwise coverage >= 0.85 at level 0.9, reduced size, in CI. plots.plot_corp(result, *, scale="probability", show_decomposition=True, ax=None) draws the PAV step against the identity with the resampled band shaded and a Brier/MCB/DSC/UNC stats box; new docs figure corp.png and chapter concepts/corp.md
  • MCB-DSC plane. plots.plot_mcb_dsc(candidates, *, score="brier", ax=None): the MCB-DSC plane — each candidate plotted at (DSC, MCB) from its CORP decomposition, with dashed iso-score diagonals MCB = DSC + (S̄ - UNC) so candidates tying on the aggregate score but splitting differently between discrimination and miscalibration are visually distinguishable (lower-right is better). Accepts a {name: (y, p)} mapping (candidates must share a weighted mean y, so UNC and the diagonals are comparable) or, directly, a fitted CalibratorSelector's report_: SelectionReport gains mcb, dsc, and unc columns (None on reports predating probcal 0.3, e.g. old goldens) computed from one corp_fit/decompose call per candidate on its own out-of-fold predictions, decomposing whichever score (Brier or log loss) drove the selection criterion. New docs figure mcb_dsc.png and section in concepts/corp.md
  • Kernel reliability curves. curves.reliability_smooth (KernelReliabilityCurve): a fourth reliability construction whose bandwidth is not a free parameter — it shares metrics.smooth_ece's fixed-point sigma_star and equal-width logit lattice (factored into metrics.smooth._lattice/_smece_solve, reused by both so the two cannot drift), so curve.smooth_ece reproduces the metric bit-for-bit rather than merely tracking it; event_rate and density are Nadaraya-Watson kernel estimates at that one sigma_star (falling back to direct O(n · grid) smoothing when smooth_ece's own path selection takes its exact, non-lattice route), and the seeded bootstrap ribbon (n_boot, default 100; n_boot=0 disables it) conditions on that fixed bandwidth rather than resampling it
  • Reliability plot upgrades. plots.plot_reliability: renders a KernelReliabilityCurve passed as smooth as a density-weighted variable-width curve (a LineCollection whose width tracks local prediction density) with the miscalibration area shaded against the identity, its bootstrap ribbon, and an smECE = ... readout; a new keyword-only stats (bool | MetricReport, default False) swaps the classic annotate box for one reporting n, events, intercept, slope, ICI, smECE, Brier, or — given a MetricReport — name = value [ci_low, ci_high] for whichever of those names the report carries; and a new keyword-only risk_dist ("rug" | "split" | None, default "rug") selects between the existing event/non-event rug and a 30-equal-mass-bin spike histogram of p (events up, non-events down, from a shared axis-fraction baseline), with rug=False disabling the density layer regardless of risk_dist. All three are additive: the pre-existing default call (annotate=True, rug=True, risk_dist="rug", smooth a SmoothReliabilityCurve) renders pixel-identically to 0.2.0, pinned by tests/test_plots_regression.py
  • Attributes diagram. plots.plot_attributes(y, p, *, method="binned", n_bins=10, scale="probability", sample_weight=None, ax=None): the Hsu & Murphy (1986) attributes diagram — identity, the climatology references (horizontal and vertical lines at the weighted base rate), the no-skill line y = (x + ybar) / 2, and a shaded positive-Brier-skill region (y - x)^2 <= (x - ybar)^2 (closer to the identity than to the no-resolution line), all drawn on a 400-point grid and all transformed through the package's clipped logit when scale="logit"; method="binned" overlays curves.reliability_binned as count-sized markers, method="corp" overlays the CORP PAV step fit (curves.corp_reliability(bands=None)) instead. New docs figure attributes.png (docs/scripts/generate_figures.py) and section in concepts/visualization.md
  • Murphy diagrams. metrics.murphy_curve(y, p, *, thresholds=513, sample_weight=None) -> MurphyCurve (metric catalog 38 → 40 symbols; count updated in docs/api-stability.md): the Ehm, Gneiting, Jordan & Krüger (2016) elementary score S_theta(p, y) = theta * 1{p > theta, y = 0} + (1 - theta) * 1{p <= theta, y = 1} of the "act if p > theta" decision rule, whose weighted mean across a threshold grid (thresholds: an int for linspace(0, 1, thresholds), or an explicit array) is the Murphy diagram; 2 * integral(S_theta) equals the Brier score exactly in the continuum and to within the default grid's 1e-3 budget at realistic n, computed in O(n log n + T log n) by sorting p once. plots.plot_murphy(curves, *, diff=False, n_boot=200, random_state=42, ax=None) renders a MurphyCurve or a {name: MurphyCurve} mapping as labelled lines, or — diff=True, given a {name: (y, p)} mapping of exactly two raw-data pairs (a MurphyCurve does not retain its data) — the pointwise score difference with a seeded paired-bootstrap band and a zero reference line. New docs figure murphy.png and sections in concepts/metrics.md and concepts/visualization.md
  • sklearn duck typing on the bare core. BaseCalibrator gains __sklearn_is_fitted__ and __sklearn_tags__, and Chain, LogitOffset and CalibratedModel gain __sklearn_is_fitted__. On sklearn >= 1.6 (the dunder-protocol versions) a bare probcal calibrator is therefore usable directly in every sklearn context that needs no shape translation — sklearn.base.clone, sklearn.utils.get_tags, sklearn.utils.validation.check_is_fitted, and CV loops such as cross_val_score(BetaCalibrator(), s.reshape(-1, 1), y, cv=3, scoring=<custom scorer>) — with no adapter import; contexts that need the (n, 2)/classes_ probability-matrix convention still go through probcal.sklearn, and so does older sklearn. The tags are built from sklearn's public Tags/TargetTags/InputTags constructors and state only what is true of a calibrator (estimator_type=None, requires_fit=True, target required, two_d_array=False); no _more_tags, since the pre-1.6 MRO-walking mechanism assumes BaseEstimator. The sklearn import lives inside __sklearn_tags__, so import probcal and a full fit/predict round trip stay numpy + stdlib only — pinned by a fresh-interpreter subprocess test (tests/test_import_footprint.py). New tests/test_sklearn_duck.py (skipped below sklearn 1.6) covers the tags, clone of every registered calibrator class, check_is_fitted before and after fit, and the cross_val_score claim verbatim; check_is_fitted itself applies to BaseCalibrator subclasses — it requires a fit method and the tag hook, which Chain (composed of already-fitted stages) does not have
  • Mirror conformance suite for the sklearn adapter. New tests/test_sklearn_mirror_checks.py re-implements, on valid (n,) probability data, every generic estimator check that is declared inapplicable to a score-level estimator but has a score-level analogue: fit idempotence, no mutation of the passed arrays (X, y, sample_weight and the query array), __dict__ unchanged by predict/predict_proba/transform (deep-copied snapshot, so an in-place mutation is caught too), pickle round trip for SklearnCalibrator and to_json/from_json round trip for every registered calibrator class, clone-then-fit equal to a fresh fit, subset and sample-order invariance, and integer sample_weight equal to row duplication — the last one over all 14 BaseCalibrator subclasses in the registry. Five of them (CenteredIsotonicCalibrator, ENIRCalibrator, IsotonicCalibrator, TemperatureCalibrator, VennAbersCalibrator) satisfy weighting ≡ duplication bit-for-bit; the rest are listed in a module-level _WEIGHT_DUPLICATION_TOLERANCE table with the measured deviation and the structural reason — unweighted np.quantile equal-mass edges in HistogramBinningCalibrator (1.1e-1; strategy="width" is exact) and on the Platt stage's output in ScalingBinningCalibrator (8.5e-2), SplineCalibrator's n-dependent knot count and inner-CV penalty search (1.9e-1), BBQCalibrator's equal-mass bin grids (2.8e-2), CrossVennAbersCalibrator's fold assignment (8.8e-3), CalibratorSelector's inner-CV selection (exact on this fixture, but not structurally so — held at the CV-level tolerance), and IRLS floating point for PlattCalibrator (2.5e-16), BetaCalibrator and SegmentedCalibrator (1.3e-14) — each asserted at its own tolerance, which is a measured value plus headroom rather than an error budget. The cheap conventions are mirrored too: fit returns self, fit does not overwrite __init__ parameters, check_is_fitted before and after fit, non-finite scores refused in fit and predict, float32 input giving float64 probabilities, list-valued and wrong-shaped sample_weight, the one-class-after-zero-weight-trimming refusal, Pipeline consistency, and fit_transform equal to fit().transform(). _MIRRORED_BY maps every mirrored check to its stand-in test and _NO_ANALOGUE names the rest (multiclass, container and dtype-object handling, memory layout, n_features_in_ bookkeeping, the 1-D-raises pair, the 2-D-y conversion warning, the positive-only tag), each spelled out in the module docstring; a guard test asserts the two together cover CALIBRATOR_XFAIL_CHECKS ∪ CLASSIFIER_XFAIL_CHECKS exactly, so the accounting cannot drift

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• treecf guide: the cross-repo work list is now documented as implemented in treecf 0.2.4 (provenance, score_calibrated read-out, plateau suite, matrix, docs), and the probcal[treecf]/all optional-dependency floor is raised to treecf>=0.2.4; the joint smoke tests additionally pin the read-out and the certificate provenance loop
  • CalibrationMonitor.report() now computes its post-alarm trailing-window diagnostics (delta_now, the Cox slope bootstrap CI, the Cox-vs-offset residual LR) on batches from the estimated drift onset onward instead of the full (or plug_in_window-trimmed) history — a window anchored where the evidence trail turns is more informative once an alarm has fired; when plug_in_window is also set, the window starts at the LATER of the onset and the plug_in_window trailing start, so a short plug_in_window still bounds how far back it can reach. This is the new default (recommendation_window="since_onset"); the keyword-only ctor parameter recommendation_window="trailing" is the escape hatch restoring 0.2.0 behaviour exactly for those diagnostic INPUTS — onset_label and the onset sentence in reasoning are populated under both modes, only the diagnostic window differs. The recommendation gate (tests/test_monitor_sim.py::test_recommendation_correct_on_pure_drift, ≥ 90% correct) stays green under the new default: 18/20 pure-offset runs correctly called re-offset, 20/20 pure-slope runs correctly called re-fit. New section in concepts/monitoring.md
  • Single-column score input. _validation.validate_scores now ravels a (n, 1) input before its existing checks, so a column vector — what an sklearn cross-validation loop hands an estimator — is accepted everywhere scores enter the package: every calibrator's fit/predict_proba, LogitOffset.fit, and the whole metric catalog. Strictly more inputs are accepted and none that worked before are rejected; results are bit-identical to passing the ravelled array. Every other 2-D shape still raises, now phrased "expected 1-D scores (or a single column); got shape ..."; validate_binary_y stays 1-D only
  • Per-check applicability reasons for the sklearn estimator checks. sklearn/_compat.py's blanket score-level reason is split: each of the 36 declared checks now carries its own reason naming the data that check generates ("2 standardized blob columns", "10 columns of U(0, 1) noise", "the 4 mean-centred iris columns", ...) and which part of the score-level contract it violates — the column count alone, or the value range as well. The declaration mechanism is unchanged (expected_failed_checks on sklearn >= 1.6, _more_tags()["_xfail_checks"] below it) and the set of declared checks is identical, so tests/test_sklearn.py still reports the same 40 xfails and no xpass; only the reasons read differently — "inapplicable", not "failing". docs/api-stability.md gains a "scikit-learn estimator checks" section stating the position (the generic checks' data model contains no score-level estimator, imbalanced-learn's resamplers being the precedent), and guide/sklearn.md's compliance paragraph points at it and at the mirror suite
  • guide/sklearn.md rewritten around three tiers. The chapter now leads with bare duck typing (sklearn >= 1.6, no adapter import), then SklearnCalibrator (the (n, 2)/classes_ shape convention: pipelines, VotingClassifier, stacking), then CalibratedClassifier (out-of-fold orchestration as one auditable object), plus the prefit recipe — CalibratedClassifierCV(FrozenEstimator(model)) and the three-line FrozenEstimator + SklearnCalibrator composition as the primitives-first alternative to CalibratedClassifier(cv="prefit"). One paragraph states the design position: the core is duck-typed to sklearn's semantic contract by design, the adapter translates shape conventions, and duck typing cannot dissolve conventions about array shapes. Every fenced code block in the chapter (9 of 9) is an --8<-- include from tests/test_sklearn_guide_snippets.py (pymdownx.snippets, with dedent_subsections: true for copy-pasteable output and check_paths: true so mkdocs build --strict fails if a snippet ever goes missing) rather than pasted, so the guide cannot drift from what is actually run — including the grid-search and metadata-routing examples, one of which previously passed calibrator=None to a GridSearchCV grid searching calibrator__variant and would have raised AttributeError on first use; the sample-weight/routing section and the compliance pointer are otherwise unchanged. CalibratedClassifier.to_json(path=None, *, indent=2) now delegates to calibrator_.to_json(...) like its other protocol methods (previously only to_dict was delegated; the guide's tier-3 example calls it directly)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• PlattCalibrator's smoothing prior now reads weighted class mass. The Lin–Lin–Weng targets (N+ + 1)/(N+ + 2) and 1/(N- + 2) took N+/N- as raw row counts while the IRLS around them was weighted, so a weighted fit used a prior built for a different sample size: integer weights did not equal row duplication (2.0e-2 apart on the mirror-suite fixture). N+/N- are now the weighted class totals, which are the row counts under unit weights — so every unweighted fit, every default, and every golden file is bit-identical (pinned by a new tests/test_parametric.py::test_platt_unit_weights_equal_no_weights), while weighting a row now matches repeating it to 2.5e-16 (test_platt_integer_weights_equal_row_duplication, and PlattCalibrator moves to the floating-point tier of the mirror suite's tolerance table). ScalingBinningCalibrator, whose first stage is a Platt fit, keeps its 8.5e-2 deviation: after this fix that is entirely the equal-mass bins on the Platt output, and its documented reason says so
  • Sample-weight delivery into CalibratedClassifier's inner fits. CalibratedClassifier.fit(X, y, sample_weight=w) raised TypeError whenever the base estimator's fit had no sample_weight parameter (KNeighborsClassifier, a Pipeline without metadata routing, ...): the weights were passed to cross_val_predict unconditionally, and the full-data refit only recovered through a bare except TypeError. It now checks first — has_fit_parameter, sklearn's own precedent in CalibratedClassifierCV, widened under metadata routing so that a router base (which takes weights through **params, not a named argument) still counts as weight-capable — and, when the base cannot take weights, warns once (UserWarning naming the class), runs the fold fits and the refit unweighted, and fits the calibrator with the weights. The silent except TypeError refit fallback is gone. Everything else was already correct and is now pinned rather than changed: with routing off, cross_val_predict(params=...) hands the weights straight to the base estimator's fit (all 3 fold fits plus the refit, verified with a spy estimator); with routing on, a Pipeline ending in SklearnCalibrator().set_fit_request(sample_weight=True) reproduces a hand-weighted BetaCalibrator fit bit-for-bit, and an undeclared request raises sklearn's UnsetMetadataPassedError instead of dropping the weights silently. New tests/test_sklearn_routing.py (9 tests, both routing modes) and a "Sample weights and metadata routing" section in guide/sklearn.md; behaviour verified identical on scikit-learn 1.4.2, 1.6.1 and 1.9.0

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: • metrics.evaluate's bootstrap loop now sorts each replicate by prediction once (np.argsort(..., kind="stable")) and shares that order across every metric that would otherwise sort or re-bin on its own: _math.loess and metrics.ecce gain a keyword-only presorted flag that skips their internal argsort (default False, so every direct call is byte-identical to before); ece, ece_debiased, and mce — which all bin at 15 equal-mass bins — share one _bin_gaps pass instead of three identical ones; and ece_sweep's ~99-candidate monotonicity scan reads per-bin weighted sums off prefix-sum differences at np.searchsorted(ps, edges, side="left") cut positions instead of rebuilding a length-n bin index per candidate (the quantile edges, their np.unique collapse, and the non-empty-bin filter are the originals; only best_b is decided there, and the returned value still comes from the unchanged ece(...) call at that bin count). Point estimates are unchanged bit-for-bit: they are still computed on the untouched unsorted path, pinned by tests/test_metrics_evaluate.py::test_evaluate_point_estimates_unchanged_by_e3 against a verbatim copy of the pre-change body, and by tests/test_metrics_binned.py for ece_sweep's value and its chosen best_b (portfolio sizes 500/5000, a tied-score fixture, and a non-uniform-weight fixture). Bootstrap percentile CI bounds may move in their last bits — reordering a replicate's rows reorders every weighted sum inside it — measured at most 3.9e-11 relative on a n=10,000/n_boot=1000 full-catalog run; tests/test_evaluate_groups.py's hard-coded fixture consequently pins its CI bounds at rtol=1e-9 instead of atol=1e-12 (its point values stay at atol=1e-12). Third, the LOESS anchor evaluation is vectorized on that same bootstrap path: new _math._loess_fit_sorted_vec solves the 512 anchors' tricube-weighted local fits in cache-sized blocks of whole windows (every window holds exactly r points, so the block is rectangular) instead of one Python iteration per anchor, and _math._loess_window_starts replaces the scalar two-pointer window walk with a searchsorted plus two exact-comparison sweeps that reproduce the loop's xs[i + r] - x0 < x0 - xs[i] rule verbatim — the window index is identical, tied scores included. It is wired in behind loess(..., presorted=True)'s grid_size anchor branch only: the per-observation path would gather O(n·r) and stays on the scalar loop, as does every presorted=False call. Its one intended numeric difference from the loop is that the tricube weight cubes by multiplication where the loop writes ** 3 (numpy sends ** 3 to libm pow at ten times the cost of two multiplies), which moves anchor values by at most 2.3e-16 relative on a well-conditioned window — pinned at rtol=1e-9 against the scalar loop on make_pd_portfolio n=1,000 and n=10,000 and a tied-score fixture, at both degree 0 and 1, in tests/test_math.py. That bound does not extend to a rank-deficient window (every non-zero tricube weight on one distinct score, which needs the far half of the window to sit at exactly the bandwidth): there the local-linear determinant is pure cancellation, ~1e-23 rather than 0, so the ulp-level weight difference can put the two paths on opposite sides of the abs(det) < _FPMIN guard and the values differ by O(1). The swy / sw branch — the weighted mean, what a rank-deficient local linear fit degenerates to — is the well-defined answer there, and either path may be the one that lands on it; the other divides by cancellation noise and is already arbitrary in the scalar loop, independently of this change. The guard is deliberately unchanged (touching it would move the point-estimate path), and because anchors are data quantiles the corner has not been observed to reach a reported value — zero end-to-end differences across 1,738 two-distinct-score configurations whose anchor grid straddles the gap, pinned by tests/test_math.py::test_loess_vectorized_rank_deficient_window and ..._do_not_reach_reported_values. Measured on the dev host, evaluate(n=10,000, n_boot=1000) over the full catalog fell from 304.2s to 86.9s (3.5x; 226.1s after the first two changes alone, the anchor fit accounting for the rest — 0.186s to 0.046s per call at n=10,000). A full-catalog replicate now costs 0.089s: ICI family 0.051s (58%), ece_sweep scan 0.024s (27%), intercept/slope 0.009s (10%), the whole binned ECE family 0.4ms — so metrics= excluding ici/e50/e90/emax remains the largest single lever on evaluate's cost. docs/scripts/benchmarks.py gains per-metric rows (ece, ece_sweep, ecce, ici, smooth_ece) at each size; the measured table, the evaluate docstring's Notes, concepts/metrics.md's "Computational cost" section, and tests/test_perf_smoke.py's docstring all carry the same numbers, and a new slow test test_evaluate_n10k_boot1000_under_150s pins the acceptance scale

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• concepts/conservatism.md consolidated into one chapter covering all four conservatism mechanisms — retitled "Conservatism: most-prudent PDs and margins of conservatism", with a new "When each mechanism applies" table (pluto_tasche/jeffreys_upper_bands per grade vs. monitor.moc_offset/moc_offset_from_counts portfolio-wide), a "Margin of conservatism" section with a runnable Chain([calibrator, moc_offset(mon)]) example showing MoC composes with calibration rather than replacing it, and an explicit warning that every bound on the page is a one-period estimator that understates uncertainty under cross-obligor correlation — the multi-period/correlated extension is out of scope for 0.3. Its mkdocs.yml nav entry moved to the end of Concepts, after CORP. concepts/offset.md gains an "Estimating delta with a standard error" section for estimate_offset/offset_from_estimate, noting they share _offset_mle with monitor._processes.plug_in_delta bit-for-bit. docs/notebooks/pd_end_to_end.ipynb (via docs/scripts/build_notebook.py) gains a "Conservative margins" section running pluto_tasche_from_arrays on the notebook's own grades and Chain([cal, moc_offset_from_counts(...)]). docs/api-stability.md gains an "Added in 0.3.0" running list of new public symbols and names estimate_offset/offset_from_estimate/OffsetEstimate in the probcal.__all__ bullet
  • concepts/monitoring.md reorganized so the recent additions read as one coherent chapter in build order: the e-process/CS theory, per-grade CS, the drift-onset estimate and its since-onset window, apply_recommendation's closed loop, margin-of-conservatism offsets (moved after the closed loop, with a new cross-link to concepts/conservatism.md's composition example), the fixed-sample hl_e_test audit, and the simulation tables — previously margin-of-conservatism sat between the per-grade CS and the onset estimate, out of build order. New ### Per-grade CS coverage and drift-onset localization table (docs/scripts/monitor_grade_onset_sim.py, 100 seeded runs, a full-size rerun of the constructions tests/test_monitor_grades.py/tests/test_monitor_onset.py already gate at reduced size): per-grade CS coverage 1.0000 for both the drifted and the stable grade (gate >= 0.9), onset localization median |onset-12| = 1.0 at both shift=0.6 (gated <= 2) and shift=0.4 (reported). The monitor_sim.py/hl_e_sim.py full-size tables were rerun and confirmed unchanged (the FleetReplay simulator path is untouched by these additions). docs/api-stability.md's "Added in 0.3.0" list gains MonitorStep.grade_delta_ci, MonitorReport.onset_label, and CalibrationMonitor(recommendation_window=). docs/notebooks/pd_end_to_end.ipynb (via docs/scripts/build_notebook.py) gains a "Monitoring closed loop" section: the alarmed monitor from the existing monitoring section calls apply_recommendation(), and a fresh monitor fed the offset-corrected forecasts for a further stretch of the same drift stays quiet

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Step calibrators' right generalized inverse (IsotonicCalibrator, HistogramBinningCalibrator) returned the next block's left edge — a supremum not in the preimage, so a consumer treating bounds as closed (treecf) landed one block too high; the right inverse now returns the largest float below the boundary, which is attained (caught by the joint treecf smoke test)
  • point_inverse honoured neither end of the no-silent-clamp doctrine at the probability boundary: p ∈ {0, 1} was clipped to [1e-12, 1 − 1e-12] before inversion (a finite "inverse" for an unattainable target), and a certified root with |z| > logit(1 − 1e-12) ≈ 27.63 was returned as σ(z), which rounds to 0.0/1.0 and cannot round-trip through predict_proba (target 0.998 → raw 1.0 → forward 0.17, no warning). Both now raise UnattainableTargetError: boundary targets all-or-nothing with the offending values named; over-range roots only for space="probability", with the error pointing at space="logit", where the answer is exact
  • LogitOffset.interval_inverse returned raw bounds below the 1e-12 clip (e.g. raw_lo = 4.5e-14 for target 1e-9 at delta = 10) that transform cannot round-trip; bounds beyond the representable output range [σ(δ − logit(1−1e-12)), σ(δ + logit(1−1e-12))] now collapse to the full-range sentinels (0/1, ±inf) exactly as in BaseCalibrator.interval_inverse, and an interval entirely outside that range raises UnattainableTargetError

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • smooth_ece's lattice path now engages for every call with a non-degenerate logit range instead of only n > bins, removing the size cliff at typical calibration-set sizes (0.1.3: exact path at n=4000 cost ~1s/call on the benchmark host and made evaluate(n=6000) bootstrap runs smECE-bound; n=8193 took ~2ms). Path selection is decoupled from n: bin at bins (default 8192), accept when the fixed point satisfies sigma* >= 8·width, refine adaptively once, fall back to exact only when refinement is infeasible or still under-resolved. Values for n <= bins may differ from the 0.1.2/0.1.3 exact grid at the ~1e-4 level on typical portfolios (measured ≤ 2.4e-4 on make_pd_portfolio; larger on wide clipped-logit-range data, where the exact path's fixed 257-point grid under-resolves small-sigma kernels and the lattice value — ≥ 8 samples per sigma — is the better one); bins=None recovers old values bit-for-bit

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Versioned JSON serialization on every fitted object: to_dict/from_dict/to_json/from_json with a schema-checked envelope (probcal_schema 1, probcal_version, class name, params, state, fit metadata) and a class registry for from_dict dispatch; fingerprint() (SHA-256, version- and timestamp-blind — identical fits fingerprint identically) plus fit_meta["data_fingerprint"] (permutation-invariant SHA-256 of the sorted training triple). Covers all 12 calibrators, LogitOffset, CalibratorSelector, and CalibratedModel (which stores a model reference — class name, model_id, get_params() — never the model object; reattach via from_dict(d, model=...); the ensemble flow refuses serialization). JSON only, no pickle anywhere. Compatibility promise — every 0.x release reads schema 1 — enforced by committed golden files verified in CI (tests/golden/); new docs chapter concepts/serialization.md
  • CalibratedModel(model_id=...) keyword-only constructor parameter naming the wrapped model in the serialized reference
  • probcal.monitor (numpy + stdlib): CalibrationMonitor — anytime-valid calibration monitoring by e-processes (alarm at E >= 1/alpha has type-I error <= alpha at every stopping time, Ville's inequality). Components: offset (predictable LogitOffset plug-in averaged with a ±{0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} uniform mixture), Cox shape plug-in, per-grade offset processes; time-uniform confidence sequence for the current offset by inverting shifted nulls; sticky alarm, anytime p-value, MonitorStep/MonitorReport, diagnostic re-offset/re-fit recommendation (trailing-window slope CI + Cox-vs-offset residual LR, a deliberate deviation from the literal design), JSON serialization with bit-exact resume, and plots.plot_e_process. Verified by simulation at full spec size (2000 runs × 24 batches × n=2000; table in concepts/monitoring.md): worst type-I 0.0275 vs gate 0.0597, delta=0.4 median detection delay 2 batches (gate 6), slope 0.8 delay 2 (gate 12), CS time-uniform coverage 0.992+ (gate 0.95); reduced-size gates + a simulator-vs-class cross-check run in CI. New concepts chapter concepts/monitoring.md
  • probcal.sklearn (extra probcal[sklearn], scikit-learn ≥ 1.4; import probcal stays numpy-only): SklearnCalibrator — a probcal calibrator as an sklearn estimator over a single score column (transform ends a Pipeline; input="logit" accepts raw margins exactly; the fitted probcal object is calibrator_), and CalibratedClassifier — the CalibratedClassifierCV(ensemble=False) drop-in on probcal calibrators (OOF via cross_val_predict or cv="prefit", one map, full refit; method="decision_function" maps through expit; binary only) which also exposes the probcal calibrator protocol by delegation so it can be handed straight to recourse engines. Estimator checks run in CI on sklearn 1.4 and latest, with structurally-inapplicable checks declared through sklearn's expected_failed_checks/_xfail_checks mechanisms and the reasons stated. New guide chapter guide/sklearn.md
  • probcal.Chain — model-free composition of a fitted calibrator with LogitOffset stages, exposing the full calibrator protocol (exact inverses through every stage, composed affine coefficients, concatenated interpret(), JSON serialization, fingerprints); CalibratedModel.chain_ returns the equivalent chain for handing to a recourse engine without the model
  • probcal.integrations.optbinning (extra probcal[optbinning], ≥ 0.21): calibrate_scorecard → CalibratedScorecard — calibrated PD over an untouched scorecard, points_affine_coeffs_ recovered and verified to machine precision (rounding=True warns and falls back to interval_inverse), exact masterscale from calibrated PD bands to point cut-offs, and provenance JSON binding the calibration layer to the scorecard table by fingerprint. New guide chapters guide/optbinning.md and guide/treecf.md (three recourse focus cases; treecf-side work list); probcal[treecf] extra with a joint smoke test
  • Protocol conformance suite (tests/test_calibrator_protocol.py): every inverse-capable object accepts interval_inverse(lo, hi, space="logit", buffer_logit=...) by keyword with lo=0/hi=1 → ∓inf and buffered-empty refusal; the step-calibrator generalized-inverse contract is spelled out in the inverse-maps chapter and pinned by tests
  • CalibratorSelector is now a BaseCalibrator subclass: same fit/predict_proba/interpret surface, plus inherited get_params/set_params, serialization, and the inverse-map machinery delegating to the refitted winner; is_monotone_ mirrors the winner
  • ENIRCalibrator.fit emits a single UserWarning above 50,000 unique scores stating the expected fit minutes — the path solver is quadratic in unique scores
  • README "Calibrators at a glance" table: one-line scaling note per method

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• End-to-end notebook on a rare-event portfolio (docs/notebooks/pd_end_to_end.ipynb): GBM baseline → logit-scale reliability → selection with bootstrap CIs → Jeffreys per-grade backtests → auditable offset → policy-to-raw translation and a treecf counterfactual → anytime-valid monitoring with an injected drift → JSON round-trips. Home Credit via kagglehub under the user's credentials with a documented synthetic fallback; the fallback executes in CI via a new nbmake job
  • Comparison benchmark (docs/benchmarks/comparison.md, reproducible via docs/scripts/comparison.py under probcal[bench]): probcal (beta abm, spline, IVAP, selector) vs sklearn sigmoid/isotonic, netcal BBQ/ENIR/beta, and betacal, on five OpenML datasets spanning ~1.5–30% event rates, with evaluate bootstrap CIs, Jeffreys grade pass rates, and fit times — including where probcal loses
  • Docs restructured: Guide (install/quickstart, sklearn, optbinning, treecf, monitoring, serialization), Concepts, Tutorials, Benchmarks, API reference + docs/api-stability.md (public surface, deprecation policy, support matrix). The "Decisions" nav section is not restored — commit 77018f2 removed the internal decision log from published docs
  • README front page rewritten around the wedge (regulated PD, audit trail, exact inverses, anytime-valid monitoring, numpy-only core) with the end-to-end notebook above the fold and the pypistats badge
  • Removed conversation-context phrasing from the _beta_point_inverse_z docstring; internal decision log entry 67 rephrased to match

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: • smooth_ece measures 1.0–3.6ms for n ∈ [64, 8192] on make_pd_portfolio (0.1.3: exact path, ~1s at n=4000 on the benchmark host), 3–6ms at n=10⁴–10⁵ and ~43ms at n=10⁶ (the O(n) pre-binning, unchanged from 0.1.3); observed lattice-vs-exact deviation ≤ 6.1e-5 across the swept sizes. evaluate(n=6000, n_boot=1000) measures 198.9s on the benchmark host (0.1.3: ≈10min, extrapolated from the 60s n_boot=100 measurement)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• ENIR (ENIRCalibrator) could exhaust memory well before m=50,000 because path_solutions_ retained every breakpoint's full-length solution (O(m^2) memory); the path solver now retains only the lowest-BIC max_solutions (default 256) breakpoints, bounding memory at any m; a pruning bound that skips provably negligible breakpoints previously crashed on sub-unit total sample_weight (log(total weight) <= 0) — the bound is now disabled in that case instead of raising, regression-tested against a sum-to-1.0 and a sum-below-1.0 case
  • sample_weight was accepted but silently had no effect on e50/e90 and on reliability_summary's internal e90 call — both now honor weights via the new Hazen-position weighted_quantile
  • evaluate's bootstrap silently substituted the point estimate for degenerate single-class i.i.d. resamples, artificially narrowing the reported CI; a degenerate draw is now redrawn (up to 100 times, then RuntimeError) instead of faked
  • CalibratorSelector's name-keyed parsimony table ranked every user-supplied candidate last on a tie regardless of actual complexity; parsimony now reads complexity_rank off the candidate instance, so a user override can win a tie against a built-in method
  • smooth_ece's binned path (default bins=8192) evaluated the smoothed measure on the exact path's 257-point grid, which aliases against the bin lattice: at small bandwidths the probe landed almost entirely between grid nodes, reporting ~1.7e-7 mass against a true total variation of 0.0749 (n=10⁴) — a spurious near-zero reading that always tripped the small-bandwidth guard and fell back to the exact O(n)-per-step computation, so every reported value stayed correct, but at a cost of ~5.7-6.1s/call regardless of n, roughly 3-6x slower than bins=None for 8192 < n ≲ 6×10⁴. The binned path now evaluates the measure natively on its own lattice by direct Gaussian convolution (closed-form total variation when the kernel is isolated, which also makes the early-exit test non-spurious by construction) with one adaptively sized refinement instead of a blind 8x retry; measured n=10⁴: ~5.7s → ~3ms; n=10⁵: 19.7s (exact) → ~10ms (default), same fixed point as exact

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• ici/e50/e90/emax and reliability_summary fit their LOESS smoother at 512 equal-mass anchors by default instead of at every observation (loess's new grid_size argument, interpolated between anchors, precedent R stats::lowess's delta); measured |Δici| ≈ 1.3e-6 on make_pd_portfolio(n=5000), far below bootstrap CI width; the underlying _loess_fit_sorted core was rewritten from an argpartition r-nearest-neighbor search to a sorted two-pointer window walk, differing from the old core only at exact distance ties (leftmost minimal-width window)
  • smooth_ece smooths a pre-binned (default bins=8192 equal-width logit bins) residual measure instead of the raw per-observation one, cutting each bisection step from 257 x n to a lattice-native evaluation independent of n, with a small-bandwidth guard (sigma* < 8 * bin_width triggers one adaptively sized refinement, bins <- ceil(range / (sigma*/8)), then a silent exact fallback if the guard still trips)
  • ENIRCalibrator.path_solutions_ is now shaped (K, m) over kept_breakpoints_ rather than every breakpoint; path_lambdas_ still records every breakpoint (pre-1.0 attribute-shape change)
  • evaluate's bootstrap resamples negative and positive classes separately by default (stratify=True), conditioning the CI on the observed class balance instead of also capturing base-rate sampling variability; stratify=False restores i.i.d. resampling
  • VennAbersCalibrator predicts from precomputed F0_/F1_ cumulative-sum-diagram sweeps fit once in fit() instead of refitting two PAVA passes per query

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• grid_size= on loess/ici/e50/e90/emax/reliability_summary and bins= on smooth_ece, both defaulting to the new fast paths; grid_size=None/bins=None recover the exact pre-0.1.3 values and cost bit-for-bit
  • evaluate keyword-only metrics= subset of the catalog — computes and bootstraps only the requested metrics instead of the full catalog, with unknown names raising ValueError
  • docs/scripts/benchmarks.py: deterministic wall-time benchmarks for ici, smooth_ece, and evaluate at several portfolio sizes; tests/test_perf_smoke.py: slow-marked regression ceilings for the grid-anchored LOESS and binned smECE fast paths
  • ENIRCalibrator(max_solutions=) (default 256) bounding retained path solutions, plus dropped_weight_ (retention loss, pruned breakpoints excluded) and kept_breakpoints_
  • VennAbersCalibrator fitted attributes F0_/F1_
  • evaluate(stratify=) keyword (default True)
  • probcal._math.weighted_quantile (Hazen positions)
  • BaseCalibrator.complexity_rank property (default 100.0), overridden by every built-in calibrator
  • ENIR/IVAP/selector rows and matching slow-marked ceilings added to the same benchmark and perf-smoke suites
  • point_inverse(p, *, space): an exact single-point preimage (calibrated probability -> raw score/logit) alongside interval_inverse's generalized-inverse interval. On BaseCalibrator, covers any affine-logit map (PlattCalibrator, TemperatureCalibrator, BetaCalibrator's tied "a"/"ab" variants) in closed form; BetaCalibrator overrides it for all three variants, including the non-affine "abm" map, via a minimax-hyperbola seed refined by up to 4 certified Halley steps; LogitOffset gets the same closed form as its interval_inverse. Non-affine monotone and step calibrators still raise NotImplementedError naming interval_inverse

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• ici at n=50,000: 192.2s (v0.1.2) to 1.2s, single-core, measured on the benchmark host
  • loess(grid_size=512) fits n=1,000,000 points in under 30s
  • ENIR fit at m=10,000: 68.6s / 783MB (v0.1.2) to 1.6s / 40.8MB tracemalloc peak, memory now bounded at any m; IVAP fit at n=100,000: 0.91s (v0.1.2 needed 188s for a fit of only 2,000 plus a predict of 10,000), predict_interval at m=100,000: 0.016s; CalibratorSelector()'s default menu: 34.5s at n=4,000 (v0.1.2) to 7.9s at n=100,000
  • evaluate's full-catalog cost at n=10⁴ was previously misattributed here to ece_sweep (~0.15s/call); the actual dominant cost pre-fix was the smooth_ece binned-path aliasing defect above (~5.7-6.1s/call, guard-triggered on every call once n > 8192). Post-fix, smooth_ece's per-call cost is negligible (a few ms up to n=10⁵); measured single-call costs at n=10⁴ / n=5×10⁴: ici 0.24s / 1.09s, ece_sweep 0.12s / 0.49s — ici, not ece_sweep, is now the largest single per-call contributor to the full-catalog cost, though neither dominates outright (together with the rest of the catalog they roughly account for the measured totals). Corrected wall times: evaluate(n_boot=100) at n=10⁴ measures ~44s, evaluate(n_boot=50) at n=5×10⁴ measures ~88s, both post-fix, driven by the catalog's ordinary O(n)-ish metrics, not by this defect; metrics= subsetting (e.g. metrics=("ici", "log_loss")) is the lever for either

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
